# Home Loan Guide

## Who is eligible for a home loan

A salaried buyer needs a minimum monthly income of 25,000 rupees. The CIBIL credit score should be 700 or above. Age must be between 21 and 60 years at the time of applying. Most banks ask for at least two years of continuous job experience. Self employed buyers need three years of income tax returns.

## How much loan will I get

buyers need three years of income tax returns.

## How much loan will I get

Banks give a maximum of 80 percent of the property value as loan. This is called loan to value ratio. As a thumb rule the loan amount is about 60 times your monthly salary. So on a salary of 50,000 rupees per month you can expect a loan of about 30 lakh. On a salary of 80,000 rupees per month you can expect a loan of about 48 lakh.

## How much down payment do I need

you can expect a loan of about 48 lakh.

## How much down payment do I need

You must pay at least 20 percent of the property price from your own pocket. The bank will never fund this part. For a 62 lakh flat the down payment is 12 lakh 40 thousand rupees. For a 45 lakh flat the down payment is 9 lakh rupees. Stamp duty and registration charges are also paid by you and are not included in the loan.

## What is the interest rate and tenure

you and are not included in the loan.

## What is the interest rate and tenure

The home loan interest rate is between 8.5 percent and 9.5 percent on floating rate. Women borrowers usually get a 0.05 percent lower rate. The maximum tenure is 30 years but most buyers choose 20 years. A longer tenure means a smaller EMI but much more total interest.

## What will my EMI be

means a smaller EMI but much more total interest.

## What will my EMI be

On a loan of 50 lakh at 9 percent interest for 20 years the EMI is about 45,000 rupees per month. On a loan of 40 lakh at 9 percent for 20 years the EMI is about 36,000 rupees per month. On a loan of 25 lakh at 9 percent for 20 years the EMI is about 22,500 rupees per month. Banks want your total EMI to stay under 50 percent of your monthly income.

## Which documents are needed for the loan

50 percent of your monthly income.

## Which documents are needed for the loan

You need PAN card, Aadhaar card, last three months salary slips, last six months bank statement, Form 16 of the last two years, and a passport size photo. For the property you need the sale agreement, the patta or title deed, and the approved building plan.

## Is there any government subsidy

title deed, and the approved building plan.

## Is there any government subsidy

Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana scheme a first time buyer from the EWS or LIG income group can get an interest subsidy of up to 2 lakh 67 thousand rupees. The buyer must not already own a pucca house anywhere in India. The property carpet area limit also applies.

## What are the extra loan charges

property carpet area limit also applies.

## What are the extra loan charges

The bank charges a processing fee of about 0.5 percent of the loan amount. On a 50 lakh loan that is 25,000 rupees. There is also a legal and technical valuation charge of around 5,000 rupees. On a floating rate loan there is no pre payment or foreclosure penalty, so you can repay early for free.

Note: these are sample figures used for a demo project. Please check with your bank for the current rates.

Stamp Duty and Registration Charges in Rajasthan
In Rajasthan the stamp duty on a property purchase is 6 percent of the registered value for
a male buyer and 5 percent for a female buyer. The registration charge is 1 percent extra.
A joint purchase by husband and wife is charged at 5.5 percent. For a 62 lakh flat
registered in a male buyer's name the stamp duty is 3 lakh 72 thousand rupees and the
registration charge is 62 thousand rupees. Stamp duty is paid on the higher of the
agreement value and the government circle rate.

GST on Property Purchase
GST applies only when you buy an under construction property from a builder. The rate is
5 percent without input tax credit, and 1 percent for an affordable house priced under 45
lakh. A ready to move flat that already has a completion certificate attracts no GST at all. A
resale flat and a plot of land also attract no GST. This is why a ready to move flat often
works out cheaper than an under construction one at the same price.

Documents Required for Registry
For the registry you need the sale deed, the patta or title deed, the approved building plan,
the latest property tax receipt, a no objection certificate from the society, the completion
certificate for a new building, PAN and Aadhaar of both buyer and seller, and two passport
size photographs. An encumbrance certificate for the last thirteen years proves that the
property has no loan or legal dispute on it.

Patta, Khatedari and Land Title
A patta is the government document that proves ownership of a plot and is issued by the
JDA, the municipal corporation or the gram panchayat. Khatedari land is agricultural land
and it must be converted to residential use before a house can be built on it. Never buy a
plot that has only khatedari rights and no patta. A JDA approved patta is the safest for a
home loan because most banks refuse to fund khatedari land.

RERA Registration and Buyer Protection
Every project with more than eight units or over 500 square metres must be registered
with Rajasthan RERA. Ask the builder for the RERA registration number and check it on
the official RERA website before booking. A RERA registered builder cannot change the
approved plan without the buyer's consent and must pay interest if possession is delayed.
You can file a complaint with RERA for a delay or a false promise.

Brokerage, Maintenance and Hidden Charges
The broker usually charges 1 percent of the property price from the buyer. A builder also
charges costs that are not in the advertised price. These are the parking charge of 2 to 5
lakh, a club membership charge, an electricity and water connection charge, and an
advance maintenance deposit of one or two years. Monthly maintenance in a Jaipur
society is around 2 to 3 rupees per square foot.

Total Cost of Buying a 62 Lakh Flat
Here is the full cost of buying the 62 lakh flat in Mansarovar. The down payment of 20
percent is 12 lakh 40 thousand rupees. The stamp duty at 6 percent is 3 lakh 72 thousand
rupees. The registration charge at 1 percent is 62 thousand rupees. The brokerage at 1
percent is 62 thousand rupees. So the total upfront money you need is about 17 lakh 36
thousand rupees. The remaining 49 lakh 60 thousand comes as a home loan and the EMI
at 9 percent for 20 years is about 44,600 rupees per month.

Note
All figures in this document are sample values used for a demo voice assistant project.
Stamp duty rates, GST rates and builder charges change from time to time. Please
confirm the current rates with the Rajasthan registration department or a property lawyer
before buying.
